newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi to seek end to Italy's metalworkers' strike.
newsitem.headline: Prodi to seek end to Italy's metalworkers' strike.

text.p: The Italian government said on Saturday it would meet with employers and trade unions next week to try and stave off a second strike in the crucial engineering and metalworkers' sectors.
Coalition parties urged Prime Minister Romano Prodi to kick start stalled negotiations between the two sides and resolve the long-running pay dispute.
Labour Minister Tiziano Treu told reporters the government had called a meeting with management and unions on Monday.
"I don't know if the strike will be avoided...but the government will certainly take steps to revive talks on the metalworkers' contract," he told reporters.
"The talks must start up again because we cannot continue in this suspended situation," he added.

The metalworkers' industry accounts for about 40 percent of total manufacturing output in Italy. Sector unions held a one-day strike in September to press their pay claim and have called another day-long stoppage for November 22.
The dispute resolves around a disagreement over how to interpret a landmark 1993 labour accord.
The accord scrapped automatic index-linking of salaries on condition that management would make up any shortfall in wages if inflation ran above target.

But the wording of the deal was deliberately vague. Unions have interpreted it to mean that all the inflation overshoot should be covered. Management argue that only a part of lost earnings need be made up.
The centre-left government has not yet said how it interprets the accord and employers have warned it to steer clear of the dispute until it makes its position clear.
